# SPE round 3 plan

Round 2 predictions lost to the naive guess in 4 of 5 rows. Round 3 therefore moves only the numbers that a round 3 change directly touches. Every other number stays at its round 2 value.

The pasted log gives priority accuracy only for C and cost only for D. My default is to predict the other A, B, C, and D cells at their r02 regraded values. I will copy those numbers from the r02 results into `spe/plans/r03.md` and `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` before the predict commit.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 3 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows that C never called the outage status check inside the merged tool. Splitting the check out tests the broken Why directly. |
| P2 | Defer to round 4 | Category accuracy of 0.86 is 14 points short of ceiling. Someone has to verify the labels on 10 new tickets. New tickets would also break the comparison with round 2 in the same round as P1 and P4. |
| P3 | Reject. Replace with a retry cap in D | D is the only low-cost config. F6 is an agent bug with a known cause, and a fix may solve it. Dropping D would remove the only cost comparison. |
| P4 | Adopt | At n=3, B's miss of 0.02 is inside noise. Five trials per cell narrows the interval. |

I will log P2 and P3 in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` as defaults, with the user as owner. The user can reverse either one before approving this plan.

### Requirements, round 3

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | In C, the outage status check becomes a separate tool again. The rest of the merged tool stays as it is. | P1, r02 F4 | The tool log shows a status check call on every outage ticket in C. |
| R3.2 | In D, the agent retries at most once per ticket. | r02 F6, P3 rejected | No D trace shows more than 1 retry. |
| R3.3 | Each cell runs 5 trials. | P4 | The harness shows 5 completed trials or 5 logged skips for every cell. |
| R3.4 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority`. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P3. The grader must score it as P3. |
| R3.5 | The ticket set stays the same as in r02. | P2 deferred | The ticket manifest hash matches the r02 hash. |
| R3.6 | A and B stay unchanged as controls. | Decision | The config diff against r02 is empty for A and B. |

## 2. Predict

Each config changes one thing. A and B change nothing. C gets R3.1. D gets R3.2.

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.80 | 0.73 | Code: `label.category` equals the answer key |
| priority accuracy | r02 value | r02 value | 0.76 | r02 value | Code: `grade.py` compares `label.priority` to the answer key |
| cost per ticket | r02 value | r02 value | r02 value + $0.0002 | $0.003 | Code: API usage tokens times the price table, divided by tickets |
| outage status check call rate (C only) | n/a | n/a | 0.95 | n/a | Code: tool log, over outage tickets only |

Why, per row:

- **Category accuracy.** A and B have no change, so they stay at 0.86. F4 concerns priority, and no round 2 evidence ties the outage check to category, so C stays at 0.80. D drops to 0.73 because some retries probably rescued long tickets, and the cap removes those rescues.
- **Priority accuracy.** C moves from 0.71 to 0.76 because outage tickets get the status check back and stop defaulting to P3. It stays below r01's 0.78 because the r01 baseline predates the F5 regrade.
- **Cost per ticket.** D moves from $0.004 back to the r01 level of $0.003 because F6 doubled tokens only through retries. C rises by about $0.0002 for one extra tool call on outage tickets.
- **Status check call rate.** C measured 0.00 in r02. A separate tool should be called on nearly every outage ticket. I allow for a few misses.

Hit tolerance is the same as in r02. Stop rule status is 0 matching rounds in a row, so the loop continues.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates before launch (all must pass)

1. **Grader selftest.** The oracle answers pass. Empty answers fail. Wrong answers fail. The F5 case from R3.4 passes.
2. **Control regrade.** Regrade the r02 transcripts with the r03 grader. It must reproduce the r02 regraded numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, D 0.74, and priority C 0.71.
3. **Dry run on 3 cells.**
   - C-T17 checks that the status check is called.
   - D on the longest ticket checks that retries are 1 or fewer.
   - A-T01 checks the baseline plumbing.
4. **Leak check.** Trials have no read path to graders, answer keys, or `spe/predictions/`.

### Workflow arguments

- `ROUND = 3`. This is a single constant. Prompt text never contains a round number written by hand.
- `configs: [A, B, C, D]`
- `tickets`: the r02 manifest, unchanged.
- `trials_per_cell: 5`
- `split_cell_extra_trials`: up to 3 more for cells with mixed pass and fail results, capped at 8 trials per cell.
- `trial_schema`: category, priority, tool_calls, retries, tokens_in, tokens_out.
- `budget_cap_usd: 5`. The harness skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip.
- After the trials, the harness scans transcripts for peeks and voids any trial that peeked.
- The workflow ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

I assume 20 tickets, because r02 reached at least T17. That gives 4 configs × 20 tickets × 5 trials = 400 trials. Agent spend at no more than $0.004 per ticket comes to about $1.60. Split cell extras add up to about $0.50. All grading is done by code, so there is no judge cost. Workflow orchestration tokens are not counted in this estimate. The $5 cap covers the agent spend.

## 4. After approval, before any harness work

1. Write the transcript to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. It holds the pasted text and "ok, next one" verbatim.
2. Append the round 3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md`, and add the P2 and P3 defaults to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1 P4, defer P2, replace P3 with D retry cap`.
3. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`.
4. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with the r02 values filled in. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` Author is "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode". Include `same_as_last_round` and a Why per number. `r03-draft.yaml` stays as it is.
5. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C splits outage check, D caps retries, n=5`.
6. Build the harness and commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`. Run the gates, then launch the workflow.
7. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
8. Close out. Update `prediction-log.md` with Which Why broke and naive versus predicted. Update `failures.md`, setting the F4 and F6 Fix fields from the results. Add a "Proposed for round 4" table, write `r04-draft.yaml`, and update `README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.

## Halt conditions

I will stop and report if any of these happens:

- The budget cap is reached.
- A trial reads the answer key.
- The control regrade does not match r02.
- A result needs a decision only the user can make.
